021/**
022 * Appenders are guaranteed to be written synchronously much like an actor in actor
023 * concurrency. They safely hold onto and communicate with the encoder and output.
024 * Appenders largely deal with correct locking, buffer reuse and flushing.
025 * {@linkplain LogAppender.AppenderFlag Flags } can be set to control the behavior the
026 * appenders and publishers can request different appender behavior through the flags.
027 *
028 * @see LogAppender.AppenderFlag
029 * @apiNote because appenders require complicated implementation and to guarantee
030 * integrity the implementations are encapsulated (sealed).
031 */
032public sealed interface LogAppender extends LogLifecycle, LogEventConsumer {
033
034        /**
035         * Default Console appender name.
036         */
037        static final String CONSOLE_APPENDER_NAME = "console";
038
039        /**
040         * Default output file appender name.
041         */
042        static final String FILE_APPENDER_NAME = "file";
043
044        /**
045         * Output appender property.
046         */
047        static final String APPENDER_OUTPUT_PROPERTY = LogProperties.APPENDER_OUTPUT_PROPERTY;
048
049        /**
050         * Encoder appender property.
051         */
052        static final String APPENDER_ENCODER_PROPERTY = LogProperties.APPENDER_ENCODER_PROPERTY;
053
054        /**
055         * Appender flags. A list of flags (usually comma separated).
056         * @see AppenderFlag
057         */
058        static final String APPENDER_FLAGS_PROPERTY = LogProperties.APPENDER_FLAGS_PROPERTY;
059
060        /**
061         * Appender type.
062         * @see AppenderType
063         */
064        static final String APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY = LogProperties.APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY;
065
066        /**
067         * Batch of events. <strong>DO NOT MODIFY THE ARRAY</strong>. Do not use the
068         * <code>length</code> of the passed in array but instead use <code>count</code>
069         * parameter.
070         * @param events an array guaranteed to be smaller than count.
071         * @param count the number of items.
072         */
073        public void append(LogEvent[] events, int count);
074
075        @Override
076        public void append(LogEvent event);
077
078        /**
079         * Boolean like flags for appender that can be set with
080         * {@link LogAppender#APPENDER_FLAGS_PROPERTY}. Unlike {@link AppenderType} more than
081         * one flag can be set at once.
082         */
083        @CaseChanging
084        public enum AppenderFlag {
085
086                /**
087                 * By default the appender will call flush on each item appended or if in async
088                 * batch mode for each batch. This flag disables that behavior so that flushing is
089                 * left up to the output (or an external mechanism) instead.
090                 */
091                DISABLE_IMMEDIATE_FLUSH,
092                /**
093                 * The appender will drop events on reentry which happens if an appender during
094                 * its append causes recursive appending in the same thread. This is an analog to
095                 * what
096                 * <a href="https://logback.qos.ch/manual/appenders.html#AppenderBase">Logback
097                 * does by default</a>. Note that this is done using {@link ReentrantLock} and not
098                 * ThreadLocal like logback <strong>and is not done by default hence the
099                 * flag!</strong>
100                 * <p>
101                 * This flag is to allow outputs that do logging themselves. For performance
102                 * reasons and to allow async publishers it is recommended that you fix the output
103                 * code such that it does not do logging. This flag is ignored if
104                 * {@link #REENTRY_LOG} is set.
105                 * <p>
106                 * <strong>This flag will not fix outputs causing lool like logging if an async
107                 * publisher is used!</strong> That is why it is recommended you fix the output by
108                 * dropping events that would cause infinite loop like logging.
109                 * @see #REENTRY_LOG
110                 */
111                REENTRY_DROP,
112                /**
113                 * The appender will log events as errors to std error on reentry which happens if
114                 * an appender during its append causes recursive appending in the same thread.
115                 * This is an analog to what
116                 * <a href="https://logback.qos.ch/manual/appenders.html#AppenderBase">Logback
117                 * does by default</a>. Note that this is done using {@link ReentrantLock} and not
118                 * ThreadLocal like logback <strong>and is not done by default hence the
119                 * flag!</strong> This flag is to resolve failures of outputs that then do
120                 * logging.
121                 * <p>
122                 * This flag takes precedence over {@link #REENTRY_DROP}.
123                 */
124                REENTRY_LOG;
125
126                static Set<AppenderFlag> parse(Collection<String> value) {
127                        if (value.isEmpty()) {
128                                return EnumSet.noneOf(AppenderFlag.class);
129                        }
130                        var s = EnumSet.noneOf(AppenderFlag.class);
131                        for (var v : value) {
132                                s.add(parse(v));
133                        }
134                        return s;
135                }
136
137                static AppenderFlag parse(String value) {
138                        String v = value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
139                        return AppenderFlag.valueOf(v);
140                }
141
142        }
143
144        /**
145         * The buffer/locking strategy an appender uses. Unlike {@link AppenderFlag} exactly
146         * one is in effect for a given appender - set on the {@link LogAppender.Builder} (or
147         * via {@link LogAppender#APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY}) at construction time and fixed for
148         * the appender's lifetime; a publisher cannot change it afterward.
149         */
150        @CaseChanging
151        public enum AppenderType {
152
153                /**
154                 * The appender will create a single buffer that will be reused and will be
155                 * protected by the appenders locking.
156                 */
157                REUSE_BUFFER,
158                /**
159                 * The appender will give each thread its own reusable buffer (a
160                 * {@link ThreadLocal}) instead of allocating a new buffer per event. Encoding is
161                 * done <strong>outside</strong> the appender's lock (the thread's buffer is only
162                 * visited by that thread so no protection is needed while encoding) with the lock
163                 * only held for the final write to the output.
164                 * <p>
165                 * The same {@link ThreadLocal} buffer is used regardless of whether the calling
166                 * thread is a platform or virtual thread. A virtual thread's entry becomes
167                 * collectible once the thread itself terminates, and a typical unit of work (e.g.
168                 * one HTTP request) logs several times on the same thread, so reusing the buffer
169                 * across those calls still pays off even for short-lived virtual threads.
170                 * <p>
171                 * This is the default type - see {@link #SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} for
172                 * the alternative lock-kind opt-in.
173                 */
174                LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER,
175                /**
176                 * Like {@link #LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} (a reused per-thread buffer, encoding
177                 * done outside any lock) except the final write to the output is protected by a
178                 * plain {@code synchronized} block (the JVM's intrinsic monitor) instead of a
179                 * {@link ReentrantLock}.
180                 * <p>
181                 * The Java language has no way to acquire a monitor in one method call and
182                 * release it in another, so this appender's critical sections are written as
183                 * literal {@code synchronized} blocks rather than going through a shared lock
184                 * abstraction the way {@link #LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} does.
185                 * {@link AppenderFlag#REENTRY_DROP} and {@link AppenderFlag#REENTRY_LOG} are
186                 * still honored though - {@link Thread#holdsLock(Object)} is the
187                 * {@code synchronized} equivalent of {@code ReentrantLock}'s
188                 * {@code isHeldByCurrentThread()}, so reentrancy is detected the same way.
189                 * <p>
190                 * Motivated by Log4j2's own garbage-free appenders using {@code synchronized}
191                 * rather than a {@code java.util.concurrent} lock around their buffer-transfer
192                 * step, and confirmed by real-workload benchmarking to outperform
193                 * {@link ReentrantLock} under platform-thread contention - this was the default
194                 * for a time. Real-workload benchmarking under virtual threads found the
195                 * opposite, a large and reproducible loss versus {@link ReentrantLock} for
196                 * reasons not fully understood (classic JEP 491 pinning was checked and ruled
197                 * out), so {@link #LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} is the default now and this type is
198                 * an opt-in for platform-thread-heavy deployments that want the edge.
199                 * <p>
200                 * <strong>Explicitly setting this type honors it</strong> even on a JDK where
201                 * {@code synchronized} still pins the carrier platform thread when called from a
202                 * virtual thread (before <a href="https://openjdk.org/jeps/491">JEP 491</a>,
203                 * finalized in JDK 24) - the one exception is
204                 * {@code LogProperties#GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY}: when that global
205                 * property is active it downgrades even an explicit request for this type to
206                 * {@link #LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER}, since its whole point is a hard guarantee
207                 * independent of anything else in the configuration.
208                 */
209                SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER,
210                /**
211                 * Like {@link #LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} (encoding done outside the lock, the
212                 * lock only guards the final write to the output) except the buffer is allocated
213                 * fresh for every single event instead of being cached in a {@link ThreadLocal}.
214                 * <p>
215                 * For deployments that want a hard guarantee of never using {@link ThreadLocal}
216                 * anywhere in the logging path - {@link #REUSE_BUFFER} is the existing
217                 * no-{@code ThreadLocal} option, but it holds its lock across the entire
218                 * encode-then-write critical section (the single shared buffer must stay
219                 * protected for as long as anything is writing into it), so it pays for that
220                 * guarantee with lock contention proportional to encoding cost, not just I/O
221                 * cost. This type keeps {@link #LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER}'s low-contention shape
222                 * (encode into a buffer nothing else can see, lock only for the write) while
223                 * dropping the {@link ThreadLocal} - the buffer is simply a local variable, not
224                 * cached anywhere, so nothing needs to be evicted or leaked-if-forgotten either.
225                 * The tradeoff is a fresh buffer allocation (and whatever it grows to internally)
226                 * on every single event instead of amortizing that allocation across a thread's
227                 * whole lifetime.
228                 * @apiNote not the default - {@link #LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER}'s reused buffer is
229                 * the better choice unless avoiding {@link ThreadLocal} entirely is a hard
230                 * requirement, not just a preference.
231                 */
232                LOCK_NEW_BUFFER;
233
234                static AppenderType parse(String value) {
235                        String v = value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
236                        return AppenderType.valueOf(v);
237                }
238
239        }
240
241        /**
242         * Creates a builder.
243         * @param name appender name.
244         * @return builder.
245         */
246        public static Builder builder(String name) {
247                return new Builder(name);
248        }
249
250        /**
251         * Builder for creating standard appenders.
252         * <p>
253         * If the output is not set standard out will be used. If the encoder is not set a
254         * default encoder will be resolved from the output.
255         */
256        public static final class Builder {
257
258                private @Nullable LogProvider<? extends LogOutput> output = null;
259
260                private @Nullable LogProvider<? extends LogEncoder> encoder = null;
261
262                private @Nullable EnumSet<AppenderFlag> flags = null;
263
264                private @Nullable AppenderType appenderType = null;
265
266                private final String name;
267
268                private Builder(String name) {
269                        this.name = name;
270                }
271
272                /**
273                 * Name of the appender.
274                 * @return name.
275                 */
276                public String name() {
277                        return this.name;
278                }
279
280                /**
281                 * Sets output.
282                 * @param output output.
283                 * @return builder.
284                 */
285                public Builder output(LogProvider<? extends LogOutput> output) {
286                        this.output = output;
287                        return this;
288                }
289
290                /**
291                 * Sets output.
292                 * @param output output.
293                 * @return builder.
294                 */
295                public Builder output(LogOutput output) {
296                        this.output = LogProvider.of(output);
297                        return this;
298                }
299
300                /**
301                 * Sets formatter as encoder.
302                 * @param formatter formatter to be converted to encoder.
303                 * @return builder.
304                 * @see LogEncoder#of(LogFormatter)
305                 */
306                public Builder formatter(LogFormatter formatter) {
307                        this.encoder = LogEncoder.of(formatter);
308                        return this;
309                }
310
311                /**
312                 * Sets formatter as encoder.
313                 * @param formatter formatter to be converted to encoder.
314                 * @return builder.
315                 * @see LogEncoder#of(LogFormatter)
316                 */
317                public Builder formatter(LogFormatter.EventFormatter formatter) {
318                        this.encoder = LogEncoder.of(formatter);
319                        return this;
320                }
321
322                /**
323                 * Sets encoder.
324                 * @param encoder encoder not <code>null</code>.
325                 * @return builder.
326                 */
327                public Builder encoder(LogProvider<? extends LogEncoder> encoder) {
328                        this.encoder = encoder;
329                        return this;
330                }
331
332                /**
333                 * Sets encoder.
334                 * @param encoder encoder not <code>null</code>.
335                 * @return builder.
336                 */
337                public Builder encoder(LogEncoder encoder) {
338                        this.encoder = LogProvider.of(encoder);
339                        return this;
340                }
341
342                /**
343                 * Sets appender flags.
344                 * @param flags flags will replace all flags currently set.
345                 * @return this.
346                 */
347                public Builder flags(Collection<AppenderFlag> flags) {
348                        _flags().addAll(flags);
349                        return this;
350                }
351
352                private EnumSet<AppenderFlag> _flags() {
353                        EnumSet<AppenderFlag> flags = this.flags;
354                        if (flags == null) {
355                                this.flags = flags = EnumSet.noneOf(AppenderFlag.class);
356                        }
357                        return flags;
358                }
359
360                /**
361                 * Adds a flag.
362                 * @param flag flag.
363                 * @return this.
364                 */
365                public Builder flag(AppenderFlag flag) {
366                        _flags().add(flag);
367                        return this;
368                }
369
370                /**
371                 * Sets the appender type (buffer/locking strategy). If not set it is resolved
372                 * from {@link LogAppender#APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY} or otherwise defaults to
373                 * {@link AppenderType#LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER}.
374                 * @param appenderType appender type.
375                 * @return this.
376                 */
377                public Builder appenderType(AppenderType appenderType) {
378                        this.appenderType = appenderType;
379                        return this;
380                }
381
382                /**
383                 * Builds.
384                 * @return an appender factory.
385                 */
386                public LogProvider<LogAppender> build() {
387                        /*
388                         * We need to capture parameters since appender creation needs to be lazy.
389                         */
390                        var _name = name;
391                        var _output = output;
392                        var _encoder = encoder;
393                        var _flags = flags;
394                        var _appenderType = appenderType;
395                        /*
396                         * TODO should we use the parent name for resolution?
397                         */
398                        return (n, config) -> {
399                                AppenderConfig a = new AppenderConfig(_name, LogProvider.provideOrNull(_output, _name, config),
400                                                LogProvider.provideOrNull(_encoder, _name, config), _flags, _appenderType);
401                                return DefaultAppenderRegistry.appender(a, config);
402                        };
403                }
404
405        }

407        /**
408         * Provides appenders safely to the publisher. The providing calls of
409         * <code>asXXX</code> can only be called once as they register the appenders.
410         */
411        class Appenders {
412
413                private final AtomicBoolean created = new AtomicBoolean();
414
415                private final String name;
416
417                private final LogConfig config;
418
419                private final List<LogProvider<LogAppender>> appenders;
420
421                Appenders(String name, LogConfig config, List<LogProvider<LogAppender>> appenders) {
422                        super();
423                        this.name = name;
424                        this.config = config;
425                        this.appenders = appenders;
426                }
427
428                /**
429                 * Return the appenders as a list.
430                 * @return list of appenders.
431                 * @throws IllegalStateException if appenders are already registered.
432                 */
433                public List<? extends LogAppender> asList() throws IllegalStateException {
434                        if (created.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
435                                var apps = appenders();
436                                List<LogAppender> appenders = new ArrayList<>();
437                                for (var a : apps) {
438                                        appenders.add(register(a));
439                                }
440                                return appenders;
441                        }
442                        else {
443                                throw new IllegalStateException("Appenders already provided.");
444                        }
445
446                }
447
448                /**
449                 * Consolidate the appenders as a single appender, appended synchronously. If more
450                 * than one appender is combined, each keeps its own independent lock and is
451                 * appended to directly - see {@link CompositeLogAppender}.
452                 * @return single appender.
453                 * @throws IllegalStateException if appenders are already registered.
454                 */
455                public LogAppender asSingle() throws IllegalStateException {
456                        if (created.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
457                                var apps = appenders();
458                                var appender = composite(apps);
459                                return register(appender);
460                        }
461                        else {
462                                throw new IllegalStateException("Appenders already provided.");
463                        }
464                }
465
466                private LogAppender register(LogAppender appender) {
467                        return switch (appender) {
468                                case DirectLogAppender ia -> {
469                                        config.serviceRegistry().put(LogAppender.class, name + "." + ia.name(), ia);
470                                        yield ia;
471                                }
472                                case CompositeLogAppender ca -> {
473                                        config.serviceRegistry().put(LogAppender.class, name, ca);
474                                        yield ca;
475                                }
476                                default -> {
477                                        throw new IllegalStateException();
478                                }
479                        };
480                }
481
482                private List<LogAppender> appenders() {
483                        return LogProvider.flatten(appenders)
484                                .describe(n -> "Appenders for route: '" + n + "'")
485                                .provide(name, config);
486                }
487
488                /**
489                 * Creates a composite log appender from many, each keeping its own independent
490                 * lock.
491                 * @param appenders appenders.
492                 * @return appender.
493                 */
494                private static LogAppender composite(List<? extends LogAppender> appenders) {
495                        if (appenders.isEmpty()) {
496                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("A single appender is required");
497                        }
498                        if (appenders.size() == 1) {
499                                return Objects.requireNonNull(appenders.get(0));
500                        }
501                        return CompositeLogAppender.of(appenders);
502                }
503
504        }
505
506        @Override
507        public void close();
508
509}

515}

520sealed interface InternalLogAppender extends LogAppender, Actor {

528         * An appender can act on actions. One of the key actions is reopening files.

531         */

536
537sealed interface DirectLogAppender extends InternalLogAppender {
538
539        String name();
540
541        LogOutput output();
542
543        LogEncoder encoder();
544
545        default List<LogResponse> _request(LogAction action) {
546                List<LogResponse> r = switch (action) {
547                        case LogAction.StandardAction a -> switch (a) {
548                                case LogAction.StandardAction.REOPEN -> List.of(reopen());
549                                case LogAction.StandardAction.FLUSH -> List.of(flush());
550                        };
551                };
552                return r;
553        }
554
555        default LogResponse reopen() {
556                var status = output().reopen();
557                return new Response(LogOutput.class, name(), status);
558        }
559
560        default LogResponse flush() {
561                output().flush();
562                return new Response(LogOutput.class, name(), LogResponse.Status.StandardStatus.OK);
563        }
564
565        static DirectLogAppender of(String name, LogOutput output, LogEncoder encoder, AppenderType type,
566                        Set<LogAppender.AppenderFlag> flags, LogAlerts alerts, LogMetrics metrics) {
567                type = AbstractLogAppender.guardSynchronizedAppenderType(type);
568                type = AbstractLogAppender.guardThreadLocalAppenderType(type);
569                return switch (type) {
570                        case REUSE_BUFFER ->
571                                new ReuseBufferLogAppender(name, output, encoder, flags, new ReentrantLock(), alerts, metrics);
572                        case SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER ->
573                                new SynchronizedThreadLocalBufferLogAppender(name, output, encoder, flags, alerts, metrics);
574                        case LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER -> new LockThreadLocalBufferLogAppender(name, output, encoder, flags,
575                                        new ReentrantLock(), alerts, metrics);
576                        case LOCK_NEW_BUFFER ->
577                                new LockNewBufferLogAppender(name, output, encoder, flags, new ReentrantLock(), alerts, metrics);
578                };
579        }
580
581}

583/**
584 * An abstract appender to help create custom appenders.
585 */
586sealed abstract class AbstractLogAppender implements DirectLogAppender {
587
588        /*
589         * Set once from LogProperties#GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY during
590         * LogConfig construction (see DefaultLogConfig) - a global, process-wide guarantee
591         * that no appender will ever use `synchronized`, for deployments that want that
592         * guaranteed even when something explicitly requests
593         * SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER. Global (not per-route/per-appender) by design,
594         * matching the property's own scope.
595         */
596        static volatile boolean forceReentrantLockAppenders = false;
597
598        /**
599         * Downgrades an explicit
600         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} to
601         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} if
602         * {@link #forceReentrantLockAppenders} is active - the enforcement point that makes
603         * the global no-synchronized guarantee a real guarantee rather than just a changed
604         * default.
605         * @param type type as given to an appender factory method.
606         * @return {@code type} unchanged, unless the guarantee is active and
607         * {@code SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} was requested, in which case
608         * {@code LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} instead.
609         */
610        static LogAppender.AppenderType guardSynchronizedAppenderType(LogAppender.AppenderType type) {
611                if (!forceReentrantLockAppenders || type != LogAppender.AppenderType.SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER) {
612                        return type;
613                }
614                return LogAppender.AppenderType.LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER;
615        }
616
617        /*
618         * Set once from LogProperties#GLOBAL_THREADLOCAL_DISABLED_PROPERTY during LogConfig
619         * construction (see DefaultLogConfig) - a global, process-wide guarantee that no
620         * appender will ever use ThreadLocal, for deployments that want that guaranteed even
621         * when something explicitly requests LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER (the default) or
622         * SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER. Global (not per-route/per-appender) by design,
623         * matching the property's own scope - rainbowgum-slf4j's MDC support independently
624         * reads the same property key to decide whether to disable itself too, see
625         * LogProperties#GLOBAL_THREADLOCAL_DISABLED_PROPERTY's javadoc.
626         */
627        static volatile boolean forceNoThreadLocalAppenders = false;
628
629        /**
630         * Downgrades either {@link ThreadLocal}-backed type (
631         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} or
632         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER}) to
633         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#LOCK_NEW_BUFFER} if
634         * {@link #forceNoThreadLocalAppenders} is active - the enforcement point that makes
635         * the global no-{@link ThreadLocal} guarantee a real guarantee rather than just a
636         * changed default. An explicit {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#REUSE_BUFFER} request
637         * is left as-is - it is already {@link ThreadLocal}-free, so there is nothing to
638         * downgrade.
639         * @param type type as given to an appender factory method.
640         * @return {@code type} unchanged, unless the guarantee is active and a
641         * {@link ThreadLocal}-backed type was requested, in which case
642         * {@code LOCK_NEW_BUFFER} instead.
643         */
644        static LogAppender.AppenderType guardThreadLocalAppenderType(LogAppender.AppenderType type) {
645                if (!forceNoThreadLocalAppenders) {
646                        return type;
647                }
648                return switch (type) {
649                        case LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER, SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER -> LogAppender.AppenderType.LOCK_NEW_BUFFER;
650                        case REUSE_BUFFER, LOCK_NEW_BUFFER -> type;
651                };
652        }
653
654        /**
655         * Whether an appender should drop (or drop-and-log) an append call because it is
656         * reentrant - i.e. the current thread is already inside a previous call to the same
657         * appender's write path, which happens if an output does logging itself during its
658         * own write. Shared by every appender that can detect reentrancy, regardless of
659         * whether it does so via a {@link ReentrantLock} (
660         * {@code lock.isHeldByCurrentThread()}) or a {@code synchronized} block (
661         * {@link Thread#holdsLock(Object)}) - callers pass in whichever check applies to
662         * them. Whenever this returns {@code true}, {@link LogMetrics#EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC}
663         * is incremented by {@code count} regardless of whether
664         * {@link AppenderFlag#REENTRY_LOG} is set - counting and logging/alerting are
665         * separate concerns, so the count still happens even when the drop itself is silent.
666         * @param reentrant whether the current thread already holds this appender's
667         * lock/monitor.
668         * @param flags the appender's flags.
669         * @param metrics where to record {@link LogMetrics#EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC} if events
670         * are dropped.
671         * @param count number of events that would be dropped - {@code 1} for a single event
672         * append, or the batch size for a batch append.
673         * @return {@code true} if the caller should drop the event(s) without appending.
674         */
675        static boolean shouldDropForReentry(boolean reentrant, Set<LogAppender.AppenderFlag> flags, LogMetrics metrics,
676                        int count) {
677                if (!reentrant) {
678                        return false;
679                }
680                if (flags.contains(LogAppender.AppenderFlag.REENTRY_LOG)) {
681                        Exception exception = new Exception("reentrant appender");
682                        MetaLog.error(LogAppender.class, exception);
683                        metrics.errorCounter(LogMetrics.EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC, count);
684                        return true;
685                }
686                if (flags.contains(LogAppender.AppenderFlag.REENTRY_DROP)) {
687                        metrics.errorCounter(LogMetrics.EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC, count);
688                        return true;
689                }
690                return false;
691        }
692
693        /**
694         * name.
695         */
696        protected final String name;
697
698        /**
699         * output
700         */
701        protected final LogOutput output;
702
703        /**
704         * encoder
705         */
706        protected final LogEncoder encoder;
707
708        protected final Set<LogAppender.AppenderFlag> flags;
709
710        protected final boolean immediateFlush;
711
712        /**
713         * alerts for reporting encode/write failures that this appender catches so they never
714         * propagate back to whatever application thread called logger.info(...).
715         */
716        protected final LogAlerts alerts;
717
718        /**
719         * metrics for recording counters like {@link LogMetrics#EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC}.
720         */
721        protected final LogMetrics metrics;
722
723        /**
724         * Creates an appender from an output and encoder.
725         * @param output set the output field and will be started and closed with the
726         * appender.
727         * @param encoder set the encoder field.
728         * @param alerts alerts for reporting encode/write failures.
729         * @param metrics metrics for recording counters.
730         */
731        protected AbstractLogAppender(String name, LogOutput output, LogEncoder encoder,
732                        Set<LogAppender.AppenderFlag> flags, LogAlerts alerts, LogMetrics metrics) {
733                super();
734                this.name = name;
735                this.output = output;
736                this.encoder = encoder;
737                this.flags = flags;
738                this.immediateFlush = !flags.contains(LogAppender.AppenderFlag.DISABLE_IMMEDIATE_FLUSH);
739                this.alerts = alerts;
740                this.metrics = metrics;
741        }
742
743        @Override
744        public void start(LogConfig config) {
745                output.start(config);
746        }
747
748        @Override
749        public void close() {
750                output.close();
751        }
752
753        @Override
754        public String toString() {
755                return getClass().getName() + "[name=" + name + " encoder=" + encoder + ", " + "output=" + output + ", flags="
756                                + flags + "]";
757        }
758
759        @Override
760        public String name() {
761                return this.name;
762        }
763
764        @Override
765        public LogOutput output() {
766                return this.output;
767        }
768
769        @Override
770        public LogEncoder encoder() {
771                return this.encoder;
772        }
773
774}

776/**
777 * Combines more than one appender on a route into one {@link LogAppender}. Each appender
778 * keeps the independent lock it was already constructed with, and
779 * {@link #append(LogEvent)}/{@link #append(LogEvent[], int)} skip locking at the
780 * composite level entirely and append to every component directly - so e.g. a console
781 * appender and a file appender under the same route never contend on the same lock for
782 * unrelated I/O. {@link #start(LogConfig)}/{@link #close()}/{@link #act(LogAction)} do
783 * the same - there is no composite-owned mutable state to protect, only a loop over
784 * components that already handle their own synchronization where it matters.
785 */
786@SuppressWarnings("ArrayRecordComponent")
787record CompositeLogAppender(DirectLogAppender[] appenders) implements InternalLogAppender {
788
789        public static CompositeLogAppender of(List<? extends LogAppender> appenders) {
790                @SuppressWarnings("null") // TODO Eclipse issue here
791                DirectLogAppender @NonNull [] array = appenders.stream()
792                        .map(CompositeLogAppender::cast)
793                        .toArray(i -> new DirectLogAppender[i]);
794                return new CompositeLogAppender(array);
795        }
796
797        private static DirectLogAppender cast(LogAppender appender) {
798                return (DirectLogAppender) appender;
799        }
800
801        @Override
802        public void append(LogEvent event) {
803                for (var appender : appenders) {
804                        appender.append(event);
805                }
806        }
807
808        @Override
809        public void append(LogEvent[] event, int count) {
810                for (var appender : appenders) {
811                        appender.append(event, count);
812                }
813        }
814
815        @Override
816        public void close() {
817                for (var appender : appenders) {
818                        appender.close();
819                }
820        }
821
822        @Override
823        public void start(LogConfig config) {
824                for (var appender : appenders) {
825                        appender.start(config);
826                }
827        }
828
829        @Override
830        public List<LogResponse> act(LogAction action) {
831                return Actor.act(appenders, action);
832        }
833
834        @Override
835        public String toString() {
836                return getClass().getName() + "[appenders=" + Arrays.toString(appenders) + "]";
837        }
838
839}

841sealed abstract class LockLogAppender extends AbstractLogAppender implements InternalLogAppender {
842
843        protected final ReentrantLock lock;
844
845        public LockLogAppender(String name, LogOutput output, LogEncoder encoder, Set<LogAppender.AppenderFlag> flags,
846                        ReentrantLock lock, LogAlerts alerts, LogMetrics metrics) {
847                super(name, output, encoder, flags, alerts, metrics);
848                this.lock = lock;
849        }
850
851        @Override
852        public List<LogResponse> act(LogAction action) {
853                lock.lock();
854                try {
855                        return _request(action);
856                }
857                catch (UncheckedIOException ioe) {
858                        return List.of(new Response(LogOutput.class, name, Status.ErrorStatus.of(ioe)));
859                }
860                finally {
861                        lock.unlock();
862                }
863        }
864
865        @Override
866        public void close() {
867                lock.lock();
868                try {
869                        super.close();
870                }
871                finally {
872                        lock.unlock();
873                }
874        }
875
876}

878/*
879 * The idea here is to reuse the buffer trading lock contention for less GC.
880 */
881final class ReuseBufferLogAppender extends LockLogAppender implements InternalLogAppender {
882
883        private final LogEncoder.Buffer buffer;
884
885        ReuseBufferLogAppender(String name, LogOutput output, LogEncoder encoder, Set<LogAppender.AppenderFlag> flags,
886                        ReentrantLock lock, LogAlerts alerts, LogMetrics metrics) {
887                super(name, output, encoder, flags, lock, alerts, metrics);
888                this.buffer = encoder.buffer(output.bufferHints());
889        }
890
891        @Override
892        public final void append(LogEvent event) {
893                if (shouldDropForReentry(lock.isHeldByCurrentThread(), flags, metrics, 1)) {
894                        return;
895                }
896                try {
897                        lock.lock();
898                        try {
899                                buffer.clear();
900                                encoder.encode(event, buffer);
901                                output.write(event, buffer);
902                                if (immediateFlush) {
903                                        output.flush();
904                                }
905                        }
906                        finally {
907                                lock.unlock();
908                        }
909                }
910                catch (Exception e) {
911                        alerts.error(getClass(), "appender '" + name + "' failed to append event", e);
912                        metrics.errorCounter(LogMetrics.EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC, 1);
913                }
914        }
915
916        @Override
917        public void append(LogEvent[] events, int count) {
918                if (shouldDropForReentry(lock.isHeldByCurrentThread(), flags, metrics, count)) {
919                        return;
920                }
921                try {
922                        lock.lock();
923                        try {
924                                output.write(events, count, encoder, buffer);
925                                if (immediateFlush) {
926                                        output.flush();
927                                }
928                        }
929                        finally {
930                                lock.unlock();
931                        }
932                }
933                catch (Exception e) {
934                        alerts.error(getClass(), "appender '" + name + "' failed to append batch of " + count + " event(s)", e);
935                        metrics.errorCounter(LogMetrics.EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC, count);
936                }
937        }
938
939        @Override
940        public void close() {
941                lock.lock();
942                try {
943                        super.close();
944                        buffer.close();
945                }
946                finally {
947                        lock.unlock();
948                }
949        }
950
951}
952
953/*
954 * The idea here is to encode outside the lock. Instead of allocating a fresh buffer per
955 * event or sharing (and thus serializing access to) a single buffer
956 * (ReuseBufferLogAppender), each thread gets its own buffer that only it will ever touch,
957 * so encoding never needs to be guarded by the lock at all - only the final write to the
958 * output does.
959 */
960final class LockThreadLocalBufferLogAppender extends LockLogAppender implements InternalLogAppender {
961
962        /*
963         * There is no way to enumerate every thread's buffer to close it on appender close so
964         * we rely on Buffer implementations not holding onto real resources (today they are
965         * all just wrapped in-memory builders) and let the ThreadLocal itself (and
966         * consequently the per-thread entries) become collectible once this appender is
967         * discarded.
968         */
969        // CheckerFramework's ThreadLocal stub declares T as inherently @Nullable since get()
970        // can return null before initialValue() runs, but withInitial(...) below guarantees
971        // it never does here.
972        @SuppressWarnings("nullness:type.argument")
973        private final ThreadLocal<LogEncoder.Buffer> bufferThreadLocal;
974
975        LockThreadLocalBufferLogAppender(String name, LogOutput output, LogEncoder encoder,
976                        Set<LogAppender.AppenderFlag> flags, ReentrantLock lock, LogAlerts alerts, LogMetrics metrics) {
977                super(name, output, encoder, flags, lock, alerts, metrics);
978                this.bufferThreadLocal = ThreadLocal.withInitial(() -> encoder.buffer(output.bufferHints()));
979        }
980
981        @Override
982        public final void append(LogEvent event) {
983                try {
984                        var buffer = bufferThreadLocal.get();
985                        buffer.clear();
986                        encoder.encode(event, buffer);
987                        writeLocked(event, buffer);
988                }
989                catch (Exception e) {
990                        alerts.error(getClass(), "appender '" + name + "' failed to append event", e);
991                        metrics.errorCounter(LogMetrics.EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC, 1);
992                }
993        }
994
995        private void writeLocked(LogEvent event, LogEncoder.Buffer buffer) {
996                if (shouldDropForReentry(lock.isHeldByCurrentThread(), flags, metrics, 1)) {
997                        return;
998                }
999                lock.lock();
1000                try {
1001                        output.write(event, buffer);
1002                        if (immediateFlush) {
1003                                output.flush();
1004                        }
1005                }
1006                finally {
1007                        lock.unlock();
1008                }
1009        }
1010
1011        @Override
1012        public void append(LogEvent[] events, int count) {
1013                if (shouldDropForReentry(lock.isHeldByCurrentThread(), flags, metrics, count)) {
1014                        return;
1015                }
1016                try {
1017                        lock.lock();
1018                        try {
1019                                output.write(events, count, encoder, bufferThreadLocal.get());
1020                                if (immediateFlush) {
1021                                        output.flush();
1022                                }
1023                        }
1024                        finally {
1025                                lock.unlock();
1026                        }
1027                }
1028                catch (Exception e) {
1029                        alerts.error(getClass(), "appender '" + name + "' failed to append batch of " + count + " event(s)", e);
1030                        metrics.errorCounter(LogMetrics.EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC, count);
1031                }
1032        }
1033
1034}

1040 * without paying ReuseBufferLogAppender's lock-across-the-whole-encode cost.

1104/*
1105 * Like LockThreadLocalBufferLogAppender (per-thread reused buffer, encode outside any
1106 * lock) but the final write is protected by a plain `synchronized` block on this
1107 * appender's own monitor instead of a ReentrantLock. Does not extend LockLogAppender -
1108 * there is no way to acquire a monitor in one method call and release it in another, so
1109 * this appender's critical sections are written as literal synchronized blocks instead.
1110 */
1111final class SynchronizedThreadLocalBufferLogAppender extends AbstractLogAppender implements InternalLogAppender {
1112
1113        private final Object monitor = new Object();
1114
1115        // See LockThreadLocalBufferLogAppender's identical field for why this suppression is
1116        // needed.
1117        @SuppressWarnings("nullness:type.argument")
1118        private final ThreadLocal<LogEncoder.Buffer> bufferThreadLocal;
1119
1120        SynchronizedThreadLocalBufferLogAppender(String name, LogOutput output, LogEncoder encoder,
1121                        Set<LogAppender.AppenderFlag> flags, LogAlerts alerts, LogMetrics metrics) {
1122                super(name, output, encoder, flags, alerts, metrics);
1123                this.bufferThreadLocal = ThreadLocal.withInitial(() -> encoder.buffer(output.bufferHints()));
1124        }
1125
1126        @Override
1127        public void append(LogEvent event) {
1128                try {
1129                        var buffer = bufferThreadLocal.get();
1130                        buffer.clear();
1131                        encoder.encode(event, buffer);
1132                        writeSynchronized(event, buffer);
1133                }
1134                catch (Exception e) {
1135                        alerts.error(getClass(), "appender '" + name + "' failed to append event", e);
1136                        metrics.errorCounter(LogMetrics.EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC, 1);
1137                }
1138        }
1139
1140        private void writeSynchronized(LogEvent event, LogEncoder.Buffer buffer) {
1141                if (shouldDropForReentry(Thread.holdsLock(monitor), flags, metrics, 1)) {
1142                        return;
1143                }
1144                synchronized (monitor) {
1145                        output.write(event, buffer);
1146                        if (immediateFlush) {
1147                                output.flush();
1148                        }
1149                }
1150        }
1151
1152        @Override
1153        public void append(LogEvent[] events, int count) {
1154                if (shouldDropForReentry(Thread.holdsLock(monitor), flags, metrics, count)) {
1155                        return;
1156                }
1157                try {
1158                        synchronized (monitor) {
1159                                output.write(events, count, encoder, bufferThreadLocal.get());
1160                                if (immediateFlush) {
1161                                        output.flush();
1162                                }
1163                        }
1164                }
1165                catch (Exception e) {
1166                        alerts.error(getClass(), "appender '" + name + "' failed to append batch of " + count + " event(s)", e);
1167                        metrics.errorCounter(LogMetrics.EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC, count);
1168                }
1169        }
1170
1171        @Override
1172        public void close() {
1173                synchronized (monitor) {
1174                        super.close();
1175                }
1176        }
1177
1178        @Override
1179        public List<LogResponse> act(LogAction action) {
1180                synchronized (monitor) {
1181                        try {
1182                                return _request(action);
1183                        }
1184                        catch (UncheckedIOException ioe) {
1185                                return List.of(new Response(LogOutput.class, name, Status.ErrorStatus.of(ioe)));
1186                        }
1187                }
1188        }
1189
